title: Aggrega Internal Template Context
description:
The runtime view assembled by the Go compiler and injected into Recipe and FeatureRecipe Go templates during rendering. When rendering an attachment FeatureRecipe the compiler additionally populates .attachment_name and .inject with the attachment-scoped context. For boundary-scope FeatureRecipes (spec.executionScope: boundary), the .context, .workload, .attachment_name, .inject, and .inject_raw pillars are absent and a .boundary.* pillar is populated instead — see the boundary block at the bottom of properties. This is NOT persisted to disk; it exists only in compiler memory during rendering. This schema documents the contract between the compiler and Ops template authors.

Base-rendering stage availability, in the order the stages run:
  Provides evaluation (locals preamble, then provides): node-local pillars only. A locals entry reads the entries above it in its own block; a provides template reads the node's whole resolved .locals. Self-reference banned (no provides entry reads another).
  Source resolution (locals publication + source eval): all pillars; .source and .workload absent. Those locals are published onto .locals here, then source: is evaluated against them.
  Values mapping (valuesMapping): all pillars + .source; .workload absent.
  Workload synthesis (workload eval): all pillars + .source; .workload being evaluated (absent from self-reference).
  Artifact evaluation (artifacts): all pillars + .source + .workload (fullest context).

context.description: The compiler-assembled execution context providing identity, topology, and delivery data.

instance_id.description: The absolute flattened ID of the current node (e.g., 'backend' or 'data-layer.main-db'), written into the alphabet every authored component name satisfies. Deterministic and stable across compilations for the same Aggregate. It is the name the compiler gives the resources it builds itself — a workload it synthesized, an artifact set it placed — so an address published for one of those is built from this value.

rendered_name.description: The name the provider bound to this node gives the resources it renders from source the author supplied — the name the supplied templates themselves render against, such as the release name a chart reads. Read it wherever this Recipe names a resource a supplied chart or module declared, whether in a provides entry, a valuesMapping, a workload, an artifacts entry or a pipeline step's with or when, because the provider may spell that name in a poorer alphabet than an authored component name is written in and the two then differ. Empty when the bound provider derives no such name: the resources of a synthesized workload and of a placed artifact set are named after the node's identity, so read '{{ .context.instance_id }}' for those, and a Recipe that wrote its own resource names already knows them. Reading this key where the bound provider reports no name halts the build and says which to write instead. The refusal covers the templates a Recipe writes inline; a valuesMapping, a workload or an artifacts entry supplied through '$import' is resolved only when the render reaches it, so a reference inside one of those renders as an empty value rather than halting. It is a Recipe's key and not a FeatureRecipe's: the value standing at it where an attachment renders is the HOST node's answer, from the host's own Recipe and provider, so an attachment's templates are refused the reference rather than served an answer about a different node — read '{{ .context.instance_id }}' there, which names the host component the attachment is resolving for.

labels.description: The duck-typing and ontology labels of the current node, including any mutations applied by mutator.wasm at topology construction.

annotations.description: The three cascading annotation buckets for the current node, segregated by origin.

release.description: Physical topology strings cascading from Release boundaries.

catalog.description: Immutable intrinsic traits authored by the Platform Architect in Domain 2.

aggregate.description: Cognitive metadata cascading from Aggregate subsystems.

inject.description: The pre-hydrated and intercepted delivery pipe. Starts as a compiler-generated map resolving Developer inject keys to Target provides values. Mutated in-place by the injectMapping deep-merges. By the time the Base Recipe renders, this contains the fully resolved physical strings.

env.description: Environment variable delivery. Keys are the Developer's local variable names, values are the resolved target strings.

file.description: File mount delivery. Keys are local file paths, values are the resolved target strings.

arg.description: Command-line argument delivery. Keys are flag prefixes, values are the resolved target strings.

all.description: Pre-calculated flat merge of env + file + arg + custom mechanisms. Populated after uses-inject resolution and recalculated after inject mapping. Templates use {{ toJson .context.inject.all }} for universal serialization.

additionalProperties.description: Custom injection paradigms (e.g., 'ssm_param'). Open-ended per the inject schema's additionalProperties.

uses.description: The enriched topological edge map. Keyed by the Developer's alias (e.g., 'my_db', 'my_api'). Each entry is a compiler-assembled view of the target node's identity, resolved provides, injection mapping, and cascaded annotations. This is NOT the raw IR edge — it is an enriched projection built by the compiler specifically for template consumption.

values.description: The opaque cognitive payload for this node, already validated by the schema validator at resolution. Passed through untouched.

infra.description: The physical sizing payload injected from the Release for this node. Bypasses the Developer entirely.

locals.description: The Recipe's own private state (e.g., primary_compute, volumes_path). Evaluated in the locals preamble — ahead of that node's provides — and published onto this pillar at source resolution. Each entry is a Go template evaluated against a self-contained node-local context carrying the entries of the same block resolved so far, so an entry MAY read a sibling defined ABOVE it and receives that sibling's resolved value. Author order is part of the contract wherever one entry reads another: moving a definition below its reader breaks the build. A '.locals.<key>' reference to a later entry, or to a key the block does not declare, halts. The check reads the path a reference RESOLVES to rather than the keystrokes, so it covers the direct form, a read inside a '{{ with .locals }}' block, and a read through a variable bound directly to '.locals' alike. Two spellings it does not cover: a reference whose path the template text does not decide — one reached through a function, such as 'index .locals', or through a 'with' block or a variable binding whose pipeline applies one — and a key read off a parenthesised block, '(.locals).<key>' or '($.locals).<key>', where the key hangs off the value the parentheses yield rather than off the block itself. Neither is analysed, and an absent key reached either way does not halt: it renders the literal text '<no value>' rather than nothing at all. A locals entry cannot read '.provides'. Available in provides (at provides evaluation, after the preamble), source, valuesMapping, workload, artifacts, assertions, and to downstream Wasm plugins via pipeline[].with (and pipeline[].when). Never exposed to callers.

provides.description: The Recipe's public API contract. Populated from provides evaluation. Available in base-rendering valuesMapping for self-reference (e.g., {{ .provides.host }}). NOT available within the provides template itself (the provides self-containment invariant). Callers resolve inject keys against these values.

features.description: Every attachment on this node, keyed by the instance name the author gave it. One pillar carries them all whatever they produce — an operational Feature, a credential Feature, an identity Feature — because what differs between attachments is what they produce, not how a template reads them. A Recipe reads them to adapt its rendering to the attached capabilities and to consume what an attachment publishes.

metadata.description: Release and compilation metadata providing global identity for deterministic naming. Available in all template blocks (valuesMapping, injectMapping, pipeline with).

release_name.description: The name of the Release driving this deployment (e.g., 'prod-billing'). Used by Ops to construct globally unique cloud resource names (S3 buckets, IAM roles). Combined with .context.instance_id to guarantee uniqueness across environments.

release_version.description: The semantic version of the Release.

environment.description: The environment string from the Release metadata (e.g., 'production', 'local').

aggregate_name.description: The name of the root Aggregate being compiled.

attachment_name.description: Only populated when rendering an attachment FeatureRecipe. Contains the attachment's instance name — the slot it fills in the owning entity's featuresSchema, or the free name the author gave it (e.g., 'admin_password', 'db_credentials'). Used to construct deterministic resource names (e.g., '{{ .context.instance_id }}-{{ .attachment_name }}').

inject.description: Only populated when rendering an attachment FeatureRecipe that carries an authored inject block (e.g., { env: { OPENAI_API_KEY: 'api_token' } }). Distinct from .context.inject which is the base component's pre-hydrated delivery pipe from uses edges. Evaluates to null/absent for attachments with no authored inject and for base Recipes.

all.description: Compiler-generated convenience merge of every attachment inject paradigm.

inject_raw.description: The immutable, unmutated Developer intent for the inject block. Evaluates to null if the Developer omitted the inject block entirely. Used by Ops for logical checks (e.g., {{ if not .inject_raw }}) to detect omission before the mutations of inject mapping.

steps.description: Pipeline inter-step communication. Only available inside Wasm pipeline 'with:' blocks. Each key is a pipeline step ID, containing the outputs exported by that step.

source.description: Resolved source field content. Populated at source resolution from the Recipe's source: field after Go-template evaluation. Available from values mapping onward (valuesMapping, workload, artifacts). Evaluates to null when the Recipe has no source:. String form = URI path; object form = structured source (e.g., OCI descriptor with resolved version).

workload.description: Parsed Workload spec for this node. Populated at workload synthesis from the Recipe's workload: field after Go-template evaluation + Workload JSON-schema validation (against workload-v1alpha1.schema.json). Available from artifact evaluation onward (artifacts) so artifacts can reference workload fields without duplication (e.g., a ServiceMonitor reading .workload.services.metrics.ports.prom). Evaluates to null when the Recipe has no workload: block. Template attempts to dereference .workload.* on a null value fail with a clear error at template eval time.

boundary.description: Boundary-scope context — populated only when evaluating a FeatureRecipe whose spec.executionScope is 'boundary'. Component-scope FRs do not receive this pillar; their context.instance_id, context.inject, context.uses, and the .workload pillar carry per-component data instead. Boundary-scope FRs receive .boundary.* in place of those per-component pillars.

path.description: The boundary's evaluated directory path (post-template-evaluation). Same string used for per-(path, provider) dispatch grouping at orchestrator-time.

boundary_name.description: The boundary's name (the map key in release.spec.boundaries).

components.description: Map of instance_id to ComponentInfo for every component in the boundary's subtree (recursive, includes nested-boundary components). Each entry carries the component's resolved type URI, instance ID, and provided values from per-component provides evaluation.

internal_uses_edges.description: Uses edges where source AND target are both in this boundary's subtree.

outgoing_cross_boundary_uses_edges.description: Uses edges where source is in subtree, target is outside. Used by compose-bridge: which outbound connections need the bridge to proxy.

incoming_cross_boundary_uses_edges.description: Uses edges where target is in subtree, source is outside. Used by ingress-style aggregators that need to know who's calling in.

cross_boundary_uses_edges.description: Convenience union of outgoing and incoming cross-boundary edges.

labels.description: Union of components' labels in the subtree, with author-order preservation.

annotations.description: The boundary's own annotations after the cascade resolves.

feature_attachments.description: The attachments directly attached to this boundary (for cross-attachment reference within boundary scope), in the same attachment shape .features carries.

template_attachment.description: One attachment as a template reads it: the per-instance view of an attached Feature. Every attachment exposes the same fields regardless of what it produces, so .features.<name> reads the same way whether that name is a slot the entity declared or a free attachment.

type.description: The Catalog Feature URI of the attached Feature.

resolved_version.description: The attached Feature's version after Manifest resolution — the version actually bound for this build, read as .features.<name>.resolved_version. Mirrors .context.uses.<alias>.resolved_version, so an attachment and an edge report a bound version the same way. Empty when the attachment's type resolves to no Catalog entity.

labels.description: The attached Feature's Catalog labels, carried verbatim in the order the Feature declares them — nothing is filtered, renamed or prefix-stripped, so a template reads exactly what the Feature's author wrote. Lets a template branch on what the attached Feature is rather than on its name or its URI. Mirrors .context.uses.<alias>.labels. The key is absent altogether when the Feature declares no labels and when the attachment's type resolves to no Catalog entity, so guard with `if` or range over the map before addressing an individual label.

values.description: The attachment's own developer-intent pillar, carried verbatim from the attachment declaration.

infra.description: The attachment's own operational-sizing pillar, carried verbatim from the attachment declaration.

provides.description: The resolved public contract of the FeatureRecipe bound to this attachment — the emitted resource's name, its key, an identity, and any additional produced keys — exposed to the consumer as .features.<name>.provides.<key>. The consumer reads these values instead of re-deriving the attachment's physical identity. An attachment whose bound FeatureRecipe publishes nothing carries no provides key at all rather than an empty map, so a template guards before addressing an individual key.

enriched_edge.description: A single enriched topological edge assembled by the compiler. Contains the target's resolved identity, provides, and cascaded annotations.

target.description: The absolute flattened ID of the target node (e.g., 'data-layer.main-db').

socket.description: The usesSchema category this edge belongs to (e.g., 'databases', 'apis').

source.description: The absolute flattened ID of the source (consumer) node. Populated for boundary-scope views that key per-consumer outputs by the consumer node.

source_namespace.description: Raw aggrega.ai/namespace annotation of the source endpoint (empty when absent). Opaque data for a provider's network-identity resolution; the core does not interpret it.

source_boundary_path.description: Boundary path of the source endpoint, used by a provider's no-namespace network fallback.

target_namespace.description: Raw aggrega.ai/namespace annotation of the target endpoint (empty when absent). Opaque data for a provider's network-identity resolution.

target_boundary_path.description: Boundary path of the target endpoint, used by a provider's no-namespace network fallback.

provides.description: The target node's fully resolved provides dictionary. Evaluated at provides evaluation, before inject hydration.

inject.description: The Developer's original inject mapping for this edge (keys = local variable names, values = target provides keys). This is the RAW mapping, not the resolved values.

labels.description: The target node's duck-typing and ontology labels (post-mutation from topology construction).

annotations.description: The target node's three cascading annotation buckets.

release.description: Physical topology strings from the target node's Release boundaries.

catalog.description: Immutable traits from the target node's Catalog entity.

aggregate.description: Cognitive metadata from the target node's Aggregate subsystems.

component.description: The target node's Catalog component type URI (e.g., 'core/postgres').

boundary_path.description: The target node's physical spatial hierarchy from the Release (e.g., 'aws-eks-cluster/backend-ns').

origin_feature.description: If this edge was autonomously declared by a Feature (including credential Features labeled feature.aggrega.ai/kind: secret), the Feature instance name. Null/absent for Developer-declared edges.
